Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can move to a model-fit eval:

- What you saw aligns well with our needs for personalized product recommendations and brief explanation snippets.
- Main concerns: hallucinations on rare SKUs, price/context sensitivity, and PII redaction for customer notes.

Can you send:
1) Your recommended model variants for this workload (latency vs quality tradeoffs).
2) Any benchmark links you have for similar retrieval + generation flows.

Next steps: we can fill the template this week if you share it; ideally we want a model-fit report by early next week so we can loop in Procurement.

Hi Alicia — great to meet you and Jake today, thanks for the clear recap.

Short answers & attachments below, and next steps at the end.

1) Recommended model variants:
- rw-13b (default): best balance of quality and latency for explanation snippets; recommended for baseline eval.
- rw-13b-quant8: lower cost option, good for high throughput but watch edge-case quality for rare SKUs.
- rw-opt-6.7b: faster/cheaper, useful for very short completion tasks (e.g., one-line recommendations).

2) Benchmarks & references (shared links):
- General perf: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/rw-13b-performance
- Latency/cost tradeoffs doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/optimizations/batching-quantization
3) Prompt-set template: attached Prompt_Set_Template.csv — it mirrors the format we use for model-fit evals (columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_behavior, edge_case_tag, redaction_required).

4) Redaction guidance: attached redaction_guidance.pdf (short checklist). Short version: remove direct PII (emails, exact payment details, full SSNs); keep product SKUs and category context. If you have customer notes that are needed for behavioral prompts, please provide synthetically redacted examples and mark them in the CSV.

Quality/regression note: when we run the model-fit eval we’ll surface precision metrics for entity extraction, hallucination rate on a sampled set, and a qualitative rating for explanation helpfulness. If you have SLAs around hallucination or a target F1 for entity recall, add that to the spreadsheet and we’ll prioritize those metrics.

Next steps / mutual action plan:
- You fill Prompt_Set_Template.csv with 25–50 prompts including edge cases by EOD Mon (3/2).
- We run model-fit evals on rw-13b and rw-13b-quant8 by Wed (3/4) and share a report.
- If results look good, we’ll block a time with Procurement & Security for contract discussions the following week.

Links uploaded to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_prompt_sets (I put template + our eval checklist).

Attaching: Prompt_Set_Template.csv, redaction_guidance.pdf

Let me know if you want us to run the eval against a redacted subset first (we can) — it speeds up procurement approvals.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi team — adding a quick note from the Eval/Applied ML side.

Logan covered the high level well. A few practical tips for the prompt spreadsheet to make the eval meaningful:
- Include "expected_behavior" column (what a correct answer looks like) and a short "failure_mode" note for each prompt (e.g., hallucination, price mismatch, missing related items).
- Tag edge cases explicitly (edge_case_tag) and include frequency (rare/occasional/common) so we weight the sampling properly.
- For redaction: when in doubt, replace PHI with consistent placeholders (e.g., <CUSTOMER_NAME>) and add a column that explains whether the original contained sensitive fields.

On metrics: we will produce the following in the model-fit report:
- Token latency (P50/P95),
- Cost per 1k prompts (estimate),
- Hallucination rate on sampled set,
- Entity recall (if applicable),
- Human quality score (1–5) averaged across test prompts.

If you want us to prioritize hallucination reduction over latency, tell us and we’ll bias the ranking to rw-13b and RW-13b+context-window (if we need longer context we can provision a variant).

I’ll coordinate the eval runs once the CSV is in the drive. If you prefer, we can run on a redacted subset first and then do a second pass on representative samples once Security signs off.

—Marissa
